problem.unresolved_other: {n} records fall on dates that no longer exist; choose what to do with each.
problem.tooManyNamed: Too many records change to review at once with Preserve named dates; use Preserve physical day.
problem.calendarStale: This calendar was changed elsewhere. Reload it and try again.

revisions.title: Earlier versions
revisions.help: Restoring brings back that definition and moves any records its change had moved back to their days. The current version is saved first.
revisions.none: No earlier versions yet. One is saved every time the definition changes.
revisions.noneShort: None yet. One is saved every time this changes.
editor.descriptionPlaceholder: Who uses this calendar, and since when?
sync.firstHelp: What is today’s date in this calendar? It becomes the world’s current date.
sync.help: This calendar’s date on the shared world day it’s anchored to.
sync.matchHelp: Match one date of this calendar to the same day in another calendar. Both then show every day in step.
sync.currentBoth: The world’s current date: {date} in {calendar}, {here} in this calendar.
fields.weekHelp: A week is as many days as there are weekdays here ({n}). Hiding labels elsewhere never changes timekeeping.
fields.noWeekdays: No weekdays: days are numbered within their month only.
fields.reset.continuous: Run continuously across months and years
fields.reset.month: Restart at the start of every month
fields.reset.year: Restart at the start of every year
fields.outsideWeek: Outside the week (these days have no weekday and don’t advance it)
fields.monthsHelp: {months}, in year order. The year’s length comes from these (plus leap days).
year.label: Year label
year.noZero: No year 0 — year -1 comes right before year 1
leap.title: Leap days
leap.none: No leap days: every year has the same length.
leap.help: Leap and occurrence rules count years from the chosen year (0 by default); with no year 0, year -1 is counted as 0.
preview.title: Preview
preview.outOfRange: Year {year} is outside the supported range, or doesn’t exist.
impact.title: Review this change
impact.intro: The shared world date stays on the same physical day. Only how dates are labeled in this calendar can change.
impact.physicalHelp: (recommended) — records stay on the same day; their label in this calendar changes. Other calendars are unaffected.
impact.namedHelp: — records keep their label in this calendar and move to a different physical day (so they move in every other calendar, and relative to moons).
impact.tooMany: Too many records to review one by one; use Preserve physical day.
impact.keepPhysical: {error} Keep it on its physical day ({date}).
impact.references: Rules that point at removed dates
impact.keepRefs: Keep them as they are (nothing is deleted; fix them afterwards)
impact.revisionNote: The previous definition is saved as a revision you can restore.
picker.badYearZero: That year can’t be shown (this calendar has no year 0).
picker.outOfRange: This date is outside the calendar’s supported range.
views.monthAbsent: This month doesn’t occur in year {year}.
manager.title: Calendars
manager.undoStale: The world date was changed since, so that step can’t be undone.
manager.defaultFailed: Could not change the default calendar.
manager.deleteBody: {name} goes to the Trash (Settings → Trash), where you can restore it. Its entries stay on the world’s timeline, and campaigns or season profiles that use it keep their dates.
manager.empty: Create your world’s first calendar: its weekdays, months and today’s date. Seasons, moons and other calendars can come later.
manager.weekHint: One week of this calendar is {n} days
sidebar.noSky: No suns, moons or stars in this calendar yet.
rec.enterAll_other: When all of {n} conditions become true
rec.enterAny_other: When any of {n} conditions becomes true
rec.everyAll_other: Every day all of {n} conditions hold
rec.everyAny_other: Every day any of {n} conditions holds
problem.rangeLimit: Ranges are limited to {n} days per query.
problem.repeatCalendarGone: The repeat rule points at a calendar that doesn’t exist.
problem.profileGone: A condition points at a season profile that doesn’t exist.
problem.objectGone: A condition points at a celestial object that doesn’t exist.
problem.linkedArticleGone: A linked article doesn’t exist (it may have been deleted).
day.whatToAdd: What do you want to add?
day.label: Day details
day.pickProfile: Pick a season profile to preview (none is assigned to a place here — articles choose their own).
day.skyQuiet: Nothing notable in the sky on this day.
day.addHint: Add a note, event or article link
day.nothing: Nothing recorded on this day yet.
day.wholeSeries: The entire series, every occurrence (moves to the Trash)
day.removeHelp: This removes it from the calendar. You can restore it from Settings → Trash.
entry.detail.event: Something that happens — it can last days or repeat
entry.detail.link: Tie an existing article to this day
entry.oneOf.note: One occurrence of a repeating note
entry.oneOf.event: One occurrence of a repeating event
entry.oneOf.link: One occurrence of a repeating article link
entry.pickDate: Pick a date that exists in this calendar.
entry.moveHint: Pick another day to move only this occurrence.
entry.title: Title
entry.summaryHelp: A short line. The note’s full, formatted text is written on the day itself.
entry.categoryHint: Group similar entries (Festival, War, Birthday…) and filter the calendar by them.
entry.colorHint: Marks the event on the calendar.
entry.repeatsHint: Occurrences are worked out from the rule; nothing is copied, so editing the rule updates them all.
entry.articlesHint: The people, places and organizations involved.
backlinks.title: On the calendar
rb.kind.monthly: Every N months, on a day
rb.kind.annual: Every N years, on a date
rb.weeksEquals: week(s) = every {n} physical days (festival days included)
rb.conditionalMonth: This month doesn’t occur every year; years without it are skipped.
rb.andMore: · and {n} more in the next {days} days
type.moon.label: Moon
type.moon.detail: Phases that repeat on a cycle: new, full and everything between.
type.sun.label: Sun
type.sun.detail: Lore, with optional states like eclipsed or blazing.
type.star.label: Star
type.star.detail: A star whose brightness or visibility can change.
type.constellation.label: Constellation
type.constellation.detail: Visible during part of every year.
type.planet.label: Planet
type.comet.label: Comet
type.comet.detail: Appears on a date, and may return.
type.custom.label: Custom
type.custom.detail: Anything else, with states of your own.
cel.shownInHelp: Its sky only appears in these calendars.
cel.allHelp: Every calendar, including ones created later.
cel.pickCalendars: Pick at least one calendar, or All.
cel.whatKind: What kind of object is it? It’s added to {calendar}; you can show it in other calendars too.
cel.calendarsRequired: Pick at least one calendar to show it in, or All.
cel.name: Name
cel.symbolHelp: Shown on calendar days and in the sky list. Pick one or type your own.
cel.showDayIconHelp: Turn it off for something that’s always there, like the sun. It still appears in each day’s details.
cel.prioritizeHelp: Drawn first on calendar days, so it stays visible when a day is crowded. Several prioritized objects go in alphabetical order.
cel.descriptionPlaceholder: What people know and believe about it.
cel.articlesHint: Articles about this object: its myths, the gods tied to it, the cult that watches it…
cel.deleteBody: It disappears from every calendar of the world, with its phases, special dates and linked articles (the articles themselves stay).
cel.deleteBlocked: If an event repeats on its phases it can’t be deleted; archive it instead to hide it everywhere and keep its history.
phases.tooShort: A {cycle}-day cycle is too short for {n} phases of at least one day each.
phases.quickStartHint: Pick a cycle length and a set of phases; the days are split for you. You can fine-tune them below.
phases.title: Phases
phases.hint_one: In order. The cycle is {n} day long.
phases.hint_other: In order. The cycle is {n} days long.
phases.none: No phases yet: use a quick start above, or add them one by one.
phases.name: Name
phases.anchorHint: Pick one day you know the moon’s phase on. Every other day, past and future, follows from it.
schedule.onceDetail: once, or coming back every few days, months or years
schedule.annualDetail: between two dates, like a winter constellation
sched.calendarAria: Calendar the dates are read in
sched.monthDayHelp: Only the month and day count. An end before the start runs into the next year.
sched.countedInAria: Calendar the months or years are counted in
sched.sameDayHelp: It comes back on the same day of the month; when a month is shorter, on its last day.
sched.alwaysRepeating: It has always been repeating (the date is just one of its appearances)
states.title: States
states.hint: What it can look like: Visible, Bright, Eclipsed… Leave this empty for an object that’s only lore.
states.whenHint: Each rule turns one state on for some days. Without a rule, a state never shows by itself.
exceptions.explain: Exceptions change what’s shown on chosen dates.
exceptions.title: Special dates
exceptions.hint: Force a state over a date range — a magical eclipse, a moon that stays full. Afterwards everything continues as if nothing happened.
restart.title: Restart the cycle
restart.hint: From a chosen day on, the cycle starts over with a phase you pick (after a cataclysm, say). Days before it keep their phases.
cv.lunations: Each lunation lasts about {days} across {phases} phases; the pattern repeats every {total} days ({lunations} lunations).
cv.cycle: A full cycle lasts {days} across {phases} phases.
cv.nextCycle: The next cycle, from this day
cv.noRules: No appearance rules: it isn’t tied to any dates.
cv.restarts_one: Its cycle restarts on {n} set date.
cv.restarts_other: Its cycle restarts on {n} set dates.
cv.notInSky: Not in the sky on this day.
sv.title: Season
sv.calendarHint: Calendar whose profiles can use it
sv.noPreview: No season profile is being previewed.
sv.notInSeason: Not in season on this day ({profile}).
se.appearanceHelp: How the season shows on the calendar and its year strips.
se.descriptionPlaceholder: What this season is like: weather, festivals, what people do…
se.usedInHelp: The dates it starts and ends are set in each season profile.
se.deleteBody: It’s removed for good. A season a profile still uses can’t be deleted: archive it instead.
se.title: Seasons
se.needCalendar: Create a calendar first: seasons belong to one.
se.help: Name each season and give it a color and symbol. When it starts and ends is set in a season profile.
pe.mode.sequentialDetail: Pick only the day each season starts; it lasts until the next one begins.
pe.mode.manualDetail: Pick the first and last day of each season; gaps or overlaps only if you allow them.
pe.name: Profile name
pe.descriptionPlaceholder: Where it applies, what makes it different…
pe.timingHelp: How each season’s last day is decided.
pe.allYearHint: This season lasts the whole year
pe.none: No seasons in this profile yet. Add the first one, then pick the day it starts.
pe.add: Add a season to this profile
pe.noSeasons: This calendar has no seasons yet: create them in Manage seasons.
pe.deleteBody: The profile is removed for good. Regions whose article uses it will have no seasons.
pe.pick: Pick a profile, or start a new one.
pe.title: Season profiles
pe.needCalendar: Create a calendar first: season profiles belong to one.
pe.help: When each season starts and ends. Regions pick a profile in their own article (the Season Profile field).

celIssue.anchorPick: Pick the day a phase begins (the cycle’s reference date).
celIssue.anchorGone: The reference phase no longer exists.
celIssue.restartGone: A cycle restart points to a removed phase.
celIssue.overrideOrder: An override ends before it starts.
celIssue.overrideGone: An override points to a removed state.

celIssue.scheduleGone: A schedule points to a removed state.
celIssue.cycle: A repeating appearance needs a whole-day period and a duration between 1 and that period.
celIssue.returnCalendar: A return in months or years needs the calendar to count them in.
celIssue.once: An appearance needs 1 or more days, and a repeat interval at least that long.
seasonIssue.startMonth: {season}: its start month doesn’t exist every year.
seasonIssue.endMonth: {season}: its end month doesn’t exist every year.
seasonIssue.day: {season}: {month} {day} doesn’t exist every year (it has {n} days).
seasonIssue.sameStart: {season} starts on the same day as another season.

seasonIssue.overlap: Some days belong to two seasons. Fix the overlap, or allow overlaps for this profile.
